chunks.title: Methods
chunks.text: Every number in the demo comes from these steps, implemented in `src/compute` and tested in `tests/`.

chunks.title: Methods
chunks.text:
1. **Read and crop.** Read the NISAR L2 GCOV backscatter layer (`/science/LSAR/GCOV/grids/frequencyA/HHHH`, 10 m pixels, EPSG 32646) and crop it to the AOI box. `tools/fetch_subset.py` reads only the box over HTTPS (about 45 MB per date instead of 7 GB). Every later scene is resampled to the first scene's grid by nearest neighbour (`src/acquire/nisar.py`). All scenes must come from the same track and frame. We plan to use the 18 Jun repeat cycle (8 passes over the Jamuna, see `docs/COVERAGE.md`).
2. **Decibels and speckle.** Convert linear power to dB (10·log10) and apply a 5×5 median filter.
3. **Water mask.** Pixels darker than the threshold are water. The threshold is the lowest point of the histogram between the water peak and the land peak (`valley_or_none`), per scene, unless `--threshold` is given. On 4 of our 8 dates (12 Jul, 24 Jul, 17 Aug, 29 Aug) wet land fills in that dip and there is no clear valley; those dates use the median of the dates that have one (`season_thresholds`, −15.0 dB). Without this, Otsu's method set −7.7 dB on 24 July and marked 2,021 km² (78% of the box) as water. With it, water on the 8 dates ranges from 454 km² (18 Jun) to 967 km² (24 Jul, the flood peak). Otsu's method is kept as an option but lands too high on the Jamuna: on 18 June 2026 Otsu gave −12.7 dB and marked wet fields and sandbars as water, while the valley sat at −15.0 dB between a water peak at −18.2 dB and a land peak at −10.3 dB. Water patches under 50 px are removed and land holes under 20 px are filled.
4. **Main river.** Water bodies of at least 2 km², after removing channels narrower than 200 m (`bankline.main_river`). Ponds, flooded fields and thin creeks cannot set the bank.
5. **Outer bank lines.** In every image row, the westmost and eastmost river pixel (`bankline.bank_columns`). Sandbars (chars) inside the river are ignored by construction. This matters: between 18 and 30 June 2026 rising water covered chars, and counting every land-to-water pixel reported 8,218 ha "lost" in 12 days. The outer-bank method reports 156 ha.
6. **Retreat per segment.** Each bank is cut into 500 m segments. Retreat is the median outward movement of the bank (positive = the river moved into the land). Confirmed retreat is the smaller of first→last and first→second-last, so a flood that recedes is not counted. A segment is left out (status "jump") when the bank line switched to another channel: median over 400 m, or rows disagreeing by more than 150 m. With only 2 dates, results are marked unconfirmed.
7. **Homes near the new bank.** Count building points on the land side within 200 m of the new bank, in the same segment.
8. **Risk level (starting thresholds, to tune on the back-test):**
   - red: retreat ≥ 100 m **and** at least one home near the new bank
   - amber: retreat ≥ 30 m
   - green: otherwise (not shown)

chunks.title: Methods
chunks.text: The original pixel-area method is still available with `--engine area`.

chunks.title: Known limits
chunks.text:
- **Minimum detectable change:** about 2 pixels. Our GCOV layer (frequency A) has 10 m pixels, so about 20 m.
- **Flooding vs erosion:** rising water can still push the outer bank line over low land next to the river. The last-two-dates rule reduces this but doesn't remove it. Comparing passes at a similar river level (BWDB gauge at Sirajganj) is the next improvement.
- **Channel switching:** in a braided river the outermost channel can change between passes. Those segments are reported as unreliable, never as erosion. On 18 to 30 June 2026, 52 of 206 bank segments were unreliable.
- **Wind and rain:** wind-roughened water can look bright and be missed.
- **Provisional data:** NISAR products are provisional.
- **Revisit:** NISAR repeats every 12 days, with 36 to 72 hours from acquisition to data. That supports a 2 to 4 week priority warning, not a same-night siren.
- **Missed pass:** in 2026 every repeat cycle over our reach skips one pass between late July and mid-August, so one interval is 24 days instead of 12.

chunks.title: Forecast (`src/compute/forecast.py`)
chunks.text:
Each stretch's bank position on every pass (metres into the land since 18 June) gets a Theil-Sen straight line: the median of all pairwise slopes, so one wild pass (a channel switch) does not drag it. We project the line to the next passes. The range uses the 10th to 90th percentile of the pairwise slopes. A stretch needs 4 measured passes, and a negative trend is reported as "not advancing", never as land coming back.

Back-test: we hid the last two passes (10 and 22 September), trained on the six before, and compared. Result on the 2026 run: median absolute error 17 m over 56 checks on 28 stretches (10 m on the 5 high-risk stretches), mean 45 m, and 59% of measured values inside the range. We first tried a 25th to 75th percentile range; only 34% of values fell inside, so we widened it to 10th to 90th. That choice was made after seeing the back-test, so treat the 59% as optimistic. The range is still too narrow (the target is about 80%).

Run: `python -m src.pipeline.scorecard` after `export_web`. It writes `webapp/public/data/forecast.json` and `scorecard.json`.

chunks.title: News back-test (`src/compute/hindcast.py`)
chunks.text:
`ground_truth/events.csv` holds erosion reports from Bangladeshi newspapers (Jamuna, Sirajganj, 18 June to 4 October 2026). For each report pinned to a village or a named point, we replay the season pass by pass, using only passes that existed at the time. A stretch is flagged on pass k when its confirmed retreat (the smaller of passes k-1 and k) reaches 30 m. The report counts as warned if a stretch within 1.5 km (village) or 750 m (named point) was flagged on or before the reported date.

Result on the 2026 run: 14 reports in the window. Only 2 fall near a measured outer bank: one warned 23 days before (16 days with a 7-day processing allowance) and one flagged 35 days after. Five are on char islands or banks the v1 engine does not measure. Seven name only a union, so they cannot be matched to a 500 m stretch until the team pins them on a map. Two events are far too few for a hit rate, and the page says so.

chunks.title: News back-test (`src/compute/hindcast.py`)
chunks.text:
Change from the plan: we had planned to count a report as caught only if its stretch was red at least 12 days before. Red needs 100 m of retreat plus homes, and neither on-bank stretch reached red, so under that rule both reports would count as missed. We report the watch-level (30 m) result and state the difference.

Lesson for version 2: most losses reported this monsoon were on chars, where many families live. The water masks already cover the chars; tracking char edges is the next engine.

chunks.title: Independent water check with NASA OPERA DSWx-HLS (`src/compute/validate.py`)
chunks.text:
On 29 August (Landsat) and 10 September (Sentinel-2), an optical satellite passed on the same day as NISAR. We compared our NISAR water mask with NASA JPL's OPERA DSWx-HLS surface-water map on a common grid of about 75 m (every second pixel of the NASA GIBS zoom-12 tiles). Only cells DSWx calls clearly water or clearly not water are compared; partial water and cloud are counted and left out. Cloud hid most of the box both days.

| Day | Cells compared | Same answer | OPERA water also found by NISAR | Water share NISAR / OPERA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 29 Aug 2026 | 74,507 | 94.1% | 90.1% | 32.0% / 32.6% |
| 10 Sep 2026 | 96,809 | 96.0% | 91.3% | 16.6% / 15.3% |

These numbers were computed on 13 November in the browser with a JavaScript copy of `compare` (same classes and rules), because NASA GIBS was not reachable from our build machine. `python tools/dswx_check.py` reproduces them in Python on any machine that can reach gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov.

chunks.title: Rain before each pass (`src/compute/rain.py`)
chunks.text: Daily precipitation from NASA POWER (PRECTOTCORR, MERRA-2 and GEOS-IT) at the box centre, summed over the 12 days up to each pass. The wettest window ended on 12 July (297 mm); the river was widest on 24 July. This is a hypothesis about timing, not a finding: the Jamuna rises on rain over its whole basin upstream, and one 50 km grid cell cannot show that.

chunks.title: Optical days (HLS)
chunks.text: For the optical-and-radar swipe, each pass is paired with the HLS day within 6 days that had the fewest bright, cloud-like pixels on the GIBS tile at the box centre. The choice is recorded in `data/hls_days_2026.json`.

chunks.title: What it predicts
chunks.text: For each 500 m bank stretch, the probability that the measured outer bank moves at least 30 m further inland by the next NISAR pass (about 12 days). Code: `src/compute/hazard.py`. Outputs: `webapp/public/data/hazard.json`.

chunks.title: Training data
chunks.text:
The stretch-by-pass panel from our NISAR engine (`src/compute/bankline.py`), Jamuna at Sirajganj, 8 passes from 18 June to 22 September 2026, 38 stretches the engine flagged red or amber. A row is a stretch at pass k with two earlier measured passes; the label is the bank change from pass k to pass k+1. 82 labelled rows; 40.2% of them are moves of 30 m or more.

Features (all known at pass k, except the last, which comes from the river outlook in operation):

| Feature | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| last_change_m | bank movement in the last interval |
| prev_change_m | bank movement in the interval before |
| position_m | bank position since the first pass |
| trend_m_per_12d | Theil-Sen trend of the stretch so far |
| water_km2 | river water extent in the box at pass k |
| water_change_km2 | change in water extent since the last pass |
| rain_mm | NASA POWER rain in the 12 days before pass k |
| east_bank | east (1) or west (0) bank |
| river_rising_next | river rises before the next pass (in the back-test: measured water extent; in operation: GloFAS 7-day trend) |

chunks.title: Models compared
chunks.text: Two learned models (scikit-learn, fixed seed 7): logistic regression with scaling, and gradient-boosted trees (depth 3, 150 iterations). Three baselines with no learning: the share of moves seen so far (base rate), "the last interval repeats" (persistence) and our earlier Theil-Sen trend.

chunks.title: Back-test
chunks.text:
Rolling origin: to score pass k+1 a model is trained only on labels known by pass k. Scored passes: 29 August, 10 September and 22 September (49 rows, 18 moves).

| Model | Brier (lower is better) | AUC | Precision at 0.5 | Recall at 0.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Gradient-boosted trees** | **0.190** | **0.682** | 0.833 | 0.556 |
| Logistic regression | 0.207 | 0.634 | 0.714 | 0.556 |
| Base rate | 0.263 | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Trend (Theil-Sen) | 0.367 | 0.512 | 0.500 | 0.056 |
| Persistence | 0.653 | 0.332 | 0.208 | 0.278 |

Without the river-outlook feature, the gradient-boosted model scores Brier 0.196 and AUC 0.677: the outlook helps a little. The shipped model is the gradient-boosted one, retrained on all 82 rows.

Per-stretch explanations: for each prediction, the change in probability when one feature is replaced by its training median (occlusion). The three largest effects are shown as the stretch's drivers.

chunks.title: Limits (read before using)
chunks.text:
- **Small sample.** 49 scored rows from one monsoon. The AUC of 0.68 has a wide uncertainty; treat the ranking as a triage aid, not a calibrated probability.
- **Selection.** The 38 stretches were chosen because they moved, so the base rate is far higher than for the whole river.
- **Waterline effect.** The measured bank partly follows the water: rising water moves it inland, falling water moves it back (see "Why it moves"). The label is "the measured bank moved inland", not "land was permanently lost".
- **Provisional radar.** NISAR products are provisional.
- **Next step.** Train on multi-year Sentinel-1 bank lines (2016 onward) run through the same engine, then test on NISAR 2026 as an independent year.

chunks.title: Rules
chunks.text: The model is deterministic, tested (`tests/test_shield.py`) and versioned with the code. Language models never compute or change these numbers. Alerts stay fixed templates.

chunks.title: NISAR coverage over our reaches
chunks.text:
**Decision: use track 69, frame 14 (ascending) for the Jamuna.** It has a GCOV file on all 8 dates of the 18 Jun cycle, each covering 100% of our box.

**Box changed on 10 October:** now 24.00–24.72° N, 89.60–89.92° E, to include Chauhali upazila (24°01′–24°17′ N), where most of our 2026 ground-truth events are. Still fully inside the track 69 footprint on all 8 dates (checked by `tests/test_tools.py`). The coverage table below was computed on the earlier, smaller box. Subsets fetched before this change must be fetched again.

chunks.title: GCOV check (10 October 2026)
chunks.text:
Searched ASF for NISAR L2 GCOV over `aoi/jamuna_sirajganj.geojson`, 17 June to 30 September 2026: 36 products. Coverage is the share of our box inside each granule footprint.

| Track / frame | Pass | Cycle | GCOV dates | Box covered | File size | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **69 / 14** | Ascending, 23:21 UTC | 18 Jun | **8**: 18 Jun, 30 Jun, 12 Jul, 24 Jul, 17 Aug, 29 Aug, 10 Sep, 22 Sep | **100%** | 6.7–6.9 GB | **Use this** |
| 19 / 76 | Descending, 12:42 UTC | 27 Jun | 7 dates; some dates have 2 products in different modes | 100% | 1.8–9.4 GB | Backup. Mixed modes need care |
| 170 / 14 | Ascending, 23:29 UTC | 25 Jun | 8 | 64–65% | 6.8–7.0 GB | Misses a third of the box |
| 91 / 76 | Descending, 12:34 UTC | 20 Jun | 8 | 22–34% | 7.0–8.7 GB | Not usable |

All products are processing version P05023, HH/HV (dual-pol) or quad-pol, and labelled PROVISIONAL.

The full list for track 69, with download URLs, preview URLs and footprints, is in [`docs/coverage/gcov_jamuna_track069_frame014.csv`](coverage/gcov_jamuna_track069_frame014.csv).

chunks.title: Files are large: read only the box
chunks.text:
Each GCOV granule is about 7 GB. All 8 dates on track 69 total **54 GB**. Our box is about 2% of a frame, so we never download whole files:

- `tools/fetch_subset.py` reads just the box over HTTPS with your Earthdata login and saves a small `.npz` per date in `cache/subsets/` (tens of MB each instead of 7 GB).
- `tools/browse_previews.py` makes video images from ASF's public preview PNGs (about 170 m per pixel), with no login at all.

chunks.title: First real files (10 October 2026)
chunks.text:
`tools/inspect_h5.py` on the 18 June granule confirmed the layout the reader expects:

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Backscatter layer | `/science/LSAR/GCOV/grids/frequencyA/HHHH` (also `HVHV`), float32, fill value NaN |
| Pixel size | 10 m (frequency A); a coarser 80 m copy sits in frequency B |
| Full frame | 34,200 × 33,552 pixels |
| Projection | EPSG 32646 (UTM 46N) |
| Our box (first, smaller version) | 5,114 × 2,856 pixels, 100% valid |
| HH range in the box | about −21 to +0.6 dB (2nd to 98th percentile) |
| Subset per date | about 44 MB, about 2 minutes over home internet |

chunks.title: Earlier search (9 October, GCOV + GUNW together)
chunks.text:
31 acquisition dates over the Jamuna box in 4 repeat cycles of 12 days. The raw dates are in `docs/coverage/nisar_pass_dates_*.csv`.

1. **One missed pass per cycle, all in the same window.** No cycle has a pass between 26 July and 12 August. On track 69 the gap runs from 24 July to 17 August (24 days instead of 12). The back-test and the video must not imply a pass in that window.
2. **Teesta.** The 9 October search found the 18 Jun cycle over the Teesta box too. Not yet checked for GCOV coverage there: run `tools/asf_pass_dates.py --aoi aoi/teesta_sundarganj.geojson --products GCOV`.
3. **Back-test timing.** Jotpara (GT008) happened on 25 July and was reported on 29 July. A catch needs a red flag by 17 July. Track 69 has 3 passes before that (18 Jun, 30 Jun, 12 Jul), enough for the two-date rule.

chunks.title: The synthetic demo
chunks.text: The synthetic test scenes in `src/pipeline/synthetic.py` use the 8 real dates of track 69. When real subsets are loaded, the demo takes its dates from the files.

chunks.title: NodiNajar (নদীনজর) · Riverbank early warning
chunks.text:
**Climate Shield: climate risk prediction and disaster early warning. Team AlphaMatrix.**

Every monsoon the Jamuna takes homes, schools and farmland in Sirajganj, Bangladesh, often overnight. Today families mostly learn which bank is going from the river itself, or from the newspaper afterwards.

NodiNajar watches the bank from orbit and warns before the land goes:

chunks.title: NodiNajar (নদীনজর) · Riverbank early warning
chunks.text:
1. **Sense.** NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar sees through monsoon cloud. We measure how far every 500 m stretch of the outer bank moves between passes (8 passes, 18 Jun to 22 Sep 2026).
2. **Predict.** A machine-learning model, back-tested against simple baselines, gives each stretch a probability of moving at least 30 m inland by the next pass. A daily river outlook (Copernicus GloFAS discharge, NOAA GFS rain) says whether that pass comes on a rising river.
3. **Expose.** Homes (Overture Maps), people (homes × census household size) and critical assets (OpenStreetMap) inside the forecast loss zone.
4. **Act.** Ranked priorities, a response planner that puts limited geobag crews and shelter places where they protect the most people, fixed-template Bangla/English alerts, and an AI assistant officials can question in Bangla or English.

> **Data status:** NISAR products are **provisional**. Forecasts are labelled as forecasts; people counts are estimates. The ML model is trained on one monsoon; read [`docs/MODEL_CARD.md`](docs/MODEL_CARD.md) before relying on it.

chunks.title: What's new in this build
chunks.text: This repository builds on our earlier open-source project [NodiNajar](https://github.com/Anthony-Kishan/NodiNajar) (NISAR pipeline, bank-line engine, first web app, trend forecast and news back-test). The first commit here imports that work unchanged; everything after it was built for this event:

chunks.title: What's new in this build
chunks.text:
| Module | Code | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ML erosion-hazard model | `src/compute/hazard.py` | Gradient-boosted trees vs logistic regression vs three baselines, rolling-origin back-test, per-stretch drivers (occlusion) |
| River outlook | `src/compute/outlook.py`, `tools/fetch_outlook.py` | GloFAS v4 discharge vs 30+ years of the same days, 7-day trend, peak, basin rain; escalates watch stretches when the river rises |
| Exposure | `src/compute/exposure.py`, `tools/fetch_osm_assets.py` | Homes and people inside the expected and high-end forecast zones; schools, mosques, health posts, markets |
| Response planner | `src/compute/planner.py`, `webapp/lib/shield.ts` | Allocates crews and shelter places by expected people protected; same rules in Python and TypeScript (checked equal) |
| AI assistant | `webapp/app/api/assistant/route.ts` | Tool-using Claude agent over 8 read-only tools, with retrieval over our docs and news reports and a number-grounding guardrail |
| MCP server | `mcp_server/server.py` | The same tools for Claude Desktop, Claude Code or any MCP client |
| Web app | `webapp/app/{forecast,plan,assistant}` | Forecast, Response plan and Ask NodiNajar tabs; early-warning card on the Overview |

chunks.title: Back-test result (2026 monsoon)
chunks.text:
To score a pass, the model only saw labels known before it. 49 held-out checks on 3 passes:

| Model | Brier (lower is better) | AUC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Gradient-boosted trees (shipped)** | **0.190** | **0.682** |
| Logistic regression | 0.207 | 0.634 |
| Base rate (no learning) | 0.263 | n/a |
| Theil-Sen trend (our earlier forecast) | 0.367 | 0.512 |
| Last interval repeats | 0.653 | 0.332 |

Small sample, one season, stretches selected because they moved. Limits in the model card.

chunks.title: Run it
chunks.text:
```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
pytest -q                                              # all tests should pass

chunks.title: Optional live data (free, no account or key):
chunks.text:
python tools/fetch_outlook.py                          # GloFAS discharge + GFS rain  -> data/outlook_raw.json
python tools/fetch_osm_assets.py                       # OpenStreetMap assets         -> data/osm_assets.json

chunks.title: Rebuild the outputs the app reads (webapp/public/data):
chunks.text:
python -m src.pipeline.scorecard                       # trend forecast + news back-test
python -m src.pipeline.export_shield                   # hazard, exposure, outlook, priorities
python -m src.agent.knowledge                          # knowledge base for the assistant

chunks.title: Web app
chunks.text:
cd webapp && npm install && npm run dev                # http://localhost:3000
```

**Assistant:** set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and optionally `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) in `webapp/.env.local` or in the Vercel project settings. Without a key the rest of the app works and the assistant page says it is not configured.

**MCP server:** `python -m mcp_server.server` (stdio) or `--http`. Claude Desktop config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"nodinajar": {"command": "python", "args": ["-m", "mcp_server.server"], "cwd": "/path/to/NodiNajar-Shield"}}}
```

**Deploy:** import the repo in Vercel with Root Directory `webapp`, add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

**Rebuilding the radar results from NISAR** (Earthdata login needed) is documented in [`docs/COVERAGE.md`](docs/COVERAGE.md) and [`docs/METHODS.md`](docs/METHODS.md): `tools/fetch_subset.py`, then `python -m src.pipeline.build_demo` and `python -m src.pipeline.export_web`.

chunks.title: Repository layout
chunks.text:
```
src/compute/     the science, deterministic and tested: water mask, bank lines, retreat, trend forecast,
                 news back-test, hazard model, river outlook, exposure, planner
src/agent/       assistant tools, knowledge retrieval (TF-IDF), number-grounding guardrail
src/pipeline/    exports for the web app (export_web, scorecard, export_shield)
mcp_server/      MCP server over src/agent/tools.py
tools/           NISAR coverage and box-only download, outlook and OpenStreetMap fetchers, checks
webapp/          Next.js app (MapLibre GL, deck.gl, Recharts) + /api/assistant
web/             fully offline demo (open web/index.html)
api/             FastAPI + PostGIS scaffold
ground_truth/    dated, sourced erosion reports from Bangladeshi newspapers
docs/            methods, model card, coverage, AI use log
tests/           pytest for everything in src/
```

chunks.title: Rules we follow
chunks.text:
- All numbers shown to users come from tested code in `src/compute`. **Language models never compute or invent a number.** Trained ML models are allowed when they are versioned, tested, back-tested against baselines and labelled as forecasts.
- The assistant reads data only through tools and every number in its answers is checked against the tool results.
- Alerts are fixed Bangla/English templates filled from computed numbers.
- NISAR output is labelled PROVISIONAL, forecasts MODEL FORECAST, people counts estimates.
- AI use is logged in [`docs/AI_USE.md`](docs/AI_USE.md).

chunks.title: Data and credits
chunks.text:
NASA data:

- NASA GIBS daily VIIRS (Suomi NPP) Corrected Reflectance true colour
- NASA HLS v2.0 (Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2) true colour via NASA GIBS
- NASA JPL OPERA DSWx-HLS surface water via NASA GIBS (independent check of our water masks)
- NASA POWER daily precipitation (PRECTOTCORR; MERRA-2 and GEOS-IT)

Other data:

- Copernicus Emergency Management Service GloFAS v4 river discharge, via the Open-Meteo Flood API
- NOAA GFS precipitation forecast, via the Open-Meteo API
- Overture Maps buildings; OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) for critical assets
- Bangladesh Population and Housing Census 2022 (BBS): average household size 3.98
- Basemaps: Esri World Imagery, Topographic, Street and Dark Gray Canvas; Sentinel-2 cloudless 2025 by EOX (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); Mapzen Terrain Tiles on AWS Open Data
- Bangladeshi newspaper reports of erosion, each linked in `ground_truth/events.csv`
- Software: Next.js, MapLibre GL, deck.gl, Recharts, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, h5py, MCP Python SDK; Anthropic Claude API for the assistant

chunks.title: GT009
chunks.text: GT009: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Ghat beside Sambhudia high school (300 m north, 100 m south lost); Char Salimabad north and south (Baghutia Chauhali, Sirajganj), event date 2026-06-26 (exact (Friday afternoon)), reported 2026-06-30 by Jugantor. Homes lost: at least 6 homesteads. Other losses: about 700 m of land in the past week; farmland. Notes:

chunks.title: GT010
chunks.text: GT010: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Char Girish union (Char Girish Kazipur, Sirajganj), event date 2026-06-14 (window (past two weeks before 28 Jun)), reported 2026-06-28 by Desh Rupantor. Homes lost: 30-40 homes. Other losses: about 30 more families homeless. Notes: Same events also in Ittefaq Bangla 29 Jun (https://www.ittefaq.com.bd/795978/)

chunks.title: GT011
chunks.text: GT011: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Chargirish Bazar to Bhetua; at least 16 villages in Kazipur (Char Girish Kazipur, Sirajganj), event date 2026-06-22 (window (past month before 22 Jul)), reported 2026-07-22 by The Daily Star. Homes lost: more than 300 houses (union member). Other losses: school, mosques, madrasa and market at risk. Notes:

chunks.title: GT012
chunks.text: GT012: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Government primary school building swept away (Kawakhola Sirajganj Sadar, Sirajganj), event date 2026-07-13 (on or before report date), reported 2026-07-13 by Independent TV. Homes lost: not stated. Other losses: school building. Notes:

chunks.title: GT013
chunks.text: GT013: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Kurshi and Dhitpur villages (Sonatoni Shahjadpur, Sirajganj), event date 2026-07-31 (window start (past two weeks before 14 Aug)), reported 2026-08-14 by Amar Sangbad. Homes lost: more than 200 houses. Other losses: Dhitpur-Kurshi cattle market; about 2,000 bigha farmland over three months. Notes: Also The New Nation 15 Aug (https://dailynewnation.com/news/842231 is 15 Jul; see tob.news 15 Aug https://tob.news/jamuna-swallows-homes-livelihoods-in-sirajganj/)

chunks.title: GT014

Homes lost: not stated. Other losses: houses, roads, farmland; Charagiris primary school at risk. Notes:

chunks.title: GT015
chunks.text: GT015: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Chauhali Janata High School, South Khaskaulia (100 m of land lost on its west side) (Khas Kaulia Chauhali, Sirajganj), event date 2026-09-21 (exact (Monday ~10:30, per UP chairman)), reported 2026-09-26 by Risingbd. Homes lost: not stated. Other losses: school building 15 ft from river; 295 students. Notes: Story anchor: same school area as GT008

chunks.title: GT016
chunks.text: GT016: bank erosion on the Jamuna at Kurshi, Barpakhia and Dhitpur villages (Sonatoni Shahjadpur, Sirajganj), event date 2026-09-28 (exact (Monday, morning to afternoon)), reported 2026-09-29 by Alokito Bangladesh. Homes lost: land of about 100 families that day; 400+ homes this season across Shahjadpur chars. Other losses: not stated. Notes:

chunks.title: GT017
chunks.text: GT017: embankment breach on the Jamuna at Barbaila to Boyalkandi, Chauhali-Tangail protection embankment (about 350 m at three points) (Sadia Chandpur Chauhali, Sirajganj), event date 2026-09-25 (window (past week before 2 Oct)), reported 2026-10-02 by Somoyer Konthosor. Homes lost: several homesteads. Other losses: five schools and a community clinic at risk. Notes: Also Rupali Bangladesh 3 Oct (https://www.rupalibangladesh.com/ajkerpatrika/news/170204); Sadia Chandpur village pin 24.25076, 89.76615 is not the breach site
